item.title: Micheál Martin confident he will remain Fianna Fáil leader
item.description: Fianna Fáil TDs and Senators are due to see the report into how Jim Gavin was chosen as the party's candidate for the Presidential election. The former Dublin GAA manager pulled out of November's election, less than a month into his campaign. Party leader, and Taoiseach, Micheál Martin has come under harsh criticism for the failed campaign. item.title: Overcrowding continues at local hospital
item.description: A local hospital was the fourth busiest in the country this morning. That's according to the latest figures released by the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation. Sligo University Hospital had 34 admitted patients waiting on beds this morning with 21 of those in the emergency department. Advertisement University Hospital Galway had the highest number of patients on trolleys this morning with 62.

item.title: 33 Per Cent of Fifth-Year Students Spend Over Eight Hours a Day on Their Phones
item.description: 33 per cent of fifth year students are spending more than eight hours a day on their phone. That's according to a study carried out by transition year students in south Roscommon. Young Social Innovators from Colaiste Chiarain are running a campaign aimed at reducing phone use this Christmas. item.title: 42nd anniversary of deaths of local soldier and Garda recruit in Leitrim
item.description: Today marks 42 years since two men killed during the Don Tidey kidnap in county Leitrim. Private Patrick Kelly and Garda Recruit Gary Sheehan were shot dead by the IRA in Drumcornan Wood, Ballinamore. It was during the rescue of the Quinnsworth managing director, who was abducted in Rathfarnham in Dublin on November 24, 1983, by armed members of the IRA, posing as gardai. item.title: Emergency services at the scene of vehicle fire on N5
item.description: Emergency services are currently at the scene of a vehicle fire on the N5 close to Frenchpark. The incident was reported shortly before 7.30pm this evening, when the minibus caught fire. Both the Fire Service and Gardaí are in attendance. Advertisement No one was injured. Motorists are advised to avoid the area. There are no further details at this stage.

item.title: Man’s body discovered in Longford town
item.description: An investigation is continuing into the discovery of a man's body in Longford town. The body of the man, aged in his 50s, was discovered at a premises on Tuesday morning. His remains were taken to the mortuary at thw Midland Regional Hospital in Mullingar for a post-mortem examination, the results of which will determine the course of the investigation. Advertisement The local Coroner has been notified.
